content.thinking: I caught that I'd put the digit and the name together in "503 {Gbf7d.1}", and the right form is just "{Gbf7d.1}". I'll correct it in both spots.

action_items.item: Make io-shop's account page render without the card details, instead of failing the whole request, when io-pay's card lookup returns an error.
Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to the on-call rotation so that it pages a person when it fires.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account pages failed. Account page requests errored from the onset onward.

The failed account page requests were failed card lookups. io-shop's payment provider client raised PaymentProviderFailed when its call for a shopper's card failed, and the page request failed with it.

ruled_out.what: A deploy or release of io-shop: none came back for the day before the onset.
A feature flag change: neither the change events nor the flag provider's history showed one.
Shoppers closing the connection (ClientDisconnected). Those errors came before the onset, and the next minute's log line shows account pages rendering normally.

causal_chain.step: The card lookups failed because io-pay, the third-party payment provider that IO Payments Ltd runs, began returning {Gbf7d.1} for them at the onset. The record does not show why io-pay failed.

input.cause_in_plain_words: The outside company that handles the shop's payments began refusing the shop's requests to look up shoppers' saved cards, and each time that happened the shop's account page failed along with the lookup.

contributing_factors.factor: No fallback was seen for when io-pay's card lookup fails. The account page request failed outright rather than rendering without the card details.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Account pages could still have rendered for shoppers while io-pay returned errors, with only the card details missing, so the outage would have been contained.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The HighErrorRate alert on io-shop paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A person would have learned of the outage when the alert fired and could have asked IO Payments Ltd to restore io-pay sooner, which would have shortened the incident.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent placed the start of the incident at the onset, using the service's per-minute metrics.
The Investigator Agent formed C1, which pointed at io-pay's failing card lookups. The log lines bear this out.
Argus read the flag provider's history to rule out flag changes by anyone else.
Argus declined to act on a service another company runs and named IO Payments Ltd as the party that must restore io-pay.

input.root_cause: The third-party payment provider io-pay began returning {Gbf7d.1} to io-shop's card lookups for shoppers. io-shop's payment provider client (payment_provider.py) raised each of those responses as PaymentProviderFailed, and the account page request failed with it instead of rendering.
input.still_at_risk: Account pages could keep failing for as long as io-pay keeps refusing card lookups, and any later io-pay outage could fail them the same way.
